title: The Full Adder: How a Carry Ripples Through a Chain
topic: Full adder — three inputs A, B, C_in and two outputs Sum, C_out; built from two half-adders and an OR gate; chained N times to add two N-bit numbers, with the carry rippling from least to most significant bit

beats.narration: Adding two bits is easy — but a carry can spread through every column. How does it actually move?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
One bit per column — but where does the carry go?

beats.narration: A half adder takes two bits A and B and produces a sum bit, X O R, and a carry bit, A N D. Good for one column, but it can't accept an incoming carry from the column below.

elements.content: XOR gate (shield shape) on top with A and B inputs, sum output
AND gate (D shape) below with same A and B inputs, carry output
Inputs A, B labelled on the left
Outputs sum and carry labelled on the right
sum = A ⊕ B, carry = A · B

beats.narration: Stack two half adders. The first takes A and B; the second adds C in to that partial sum. An O R gate merges the two carry signals into C out.

elements.content: Two stacked XOR gates and two AND gates, plus an OR gate at the bottom merging carries
Three inputs A, B, C_in on the left
Two outputs Sum, C_out on the right
two half adders + one OR — that's a full adder

beats.narration: Set A and B to one, and C in to one. The first X O R fires, then the second X O R fires, and finally the O R gate raises C out. Sum lands at one, C out lands at one — one plus one plus one equals binary one one.

elements.content: Full-adder diagram from beat 3, with signals propagating left to right
Input values 1, 1, 1 flash in over the input wires
Each gate glows briefly as its inputs settle
1 + 1 + 1 = 11₂ — sum 1, carry 1

beats.narration: Chain four of them and you add two four-bit numbers. The carry from each column has to settle before the next column can finish — that's why the rightmost adder fires first, then the next, and so on.

elements.content: Four full-adder blocks in a row, labelled 0 through 3, carry-out of one feeding carry-in of the next
Pulse marks travel left through the carry chain, illuminating each adder in turn
Bottom result: S = 1010 (=10₁₀), final C_out = 0

beats.narration: Each column is local. The carry chain is global — and that is what makes ripple-carry addition slow for wide numbers.

elements.content: Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ C_in
C_out = AB + C_in(A ⊕ B)
local sum, global carry — the bottleneck of ripple-carry adders
